new_items.title: The Fredholm index of a strip operator with real diagonal limits
new_items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $m\ge1$ and $0<\theta_j<\pi$. Let $X=H^1_\theta$ be the real Hilbert completion, in the norm $(\|u\|_2^2+\|u_s\|_2^2+\|u_t\|_2^2)^{1/2}$, of smooth maps on $\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$ compactly supported in $s$ and satisfying $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$, $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Put $Y=L^2(\mathbb R\times[0,1];\mathbb C^m)$, regarded as a real Hilbert space. Suppose $B(s,t)$ is an essentially bounded measurable real linear endomorphism and has real diagonal limits $B_\pm=\operatorname{diag}(b_{\pm,j})$ uniformly in essential supremum as $s\to\pm\infty$, with $\theta_j-b_{\pm,j}\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. Then the bounded Fredholm operator
$$T=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B:X\longrightarrow Y$$
has real index
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T=\sum_{j=1}^m\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{-,j}}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{+,j}}\pi\right\rfloor\right).$$
For the diagonal step function $B^0(s)=B_-$ for $s<0$ and $B_+$ for $s\ge0$, the kernel has one real generator for every $(j,n)\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\mathbb Z$ with $\lambda_{-,j,n}<0<\lambda_{+,j,n}$, and the cokernel has one for every pair with $\lambda_{-,j,n}>0>\lambda_{+,j,n}$, where $\lambda_{\pm,j,n}=\pi n-\theta_j+b_{\pm,j}$.

The same index holds on the two-sided weighted spaces $X_\delta=\{u:e^{\delta|s|}u\in X\}$ and $Y_\delta=\{f:e^{\delta|s|}f\in Y\}$ whenever $0\le\delta<\min_{j,\pm,n}|\lambda_{\pm,j,n}|$. This is an index theorem for this specified strip operator and product-line domain; it does not identify the pullback operator of a general geometric strip or assert a Heegaard-domain Maslov formula.

new_items.title: A rotating scalar strip boundary line has an explicit winding index
new_items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\vartheta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real function constant at values $\vartheta_-$ and $\vartheta_+$ on the two ends, with $\vartheta_\pm\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. On $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, let $X_\vartheta$ be the $H^1$ completion of smooth complex-valued maps compactly supported in $s$, with $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R$ and $u(s,1)\in e^{i\vartheta(s)}\mathbb R$. Let $A(s,t):\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be an essentially bounded measurable real linear map tending to zero uniformly in essential supremum on both ends. Then
$$\mathcal D=\partial_s+i\partial_t+A:X_\vartheta\longrightarrow L^2(S;\mathbb C)$$
is bounded Fredholm over $\mathbb R$, before taking any quotient by translation, and
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}\mathcal D=\left\lfloor\frac{\vartheta_-}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\vartheta_+}\pi\right\rfloor.$$
The same index holds on the spaces weighted by $e^{\delta|s|}$ when $0\le\delta<\min_{\pm}\operatorname{dist}(\vartheta_\pm,\pi\mathbb Z)$. In particular, if the upper line is the same at both ends and $\vartheta_+-\vartheta_-=k\pi$, its fixed-end strip index is $-k$. This sign uses the orientation $ds\wedge dt$ and the operator $\partial_s+i\partial_t$: the oriented upper boundary runs from $s=+\infty$ to $s=-\infty$.

Componentwise the same result holds for finitely many given angle functions $\vartheta_j(s)$, the product upper boundary $\prod_j e^{i\vartheta_j(s)}\mathbb R$, and any bounded real linear matrix $A(s,t)$ tending to zero: the real index is the sum of their displayed floor differences. This is an explicit globally framed boundary-line result; it does not supply a global frame for a general geometric strip or identify its index with a Heegaard-domain expression.
